turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, then select the 5
candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20 pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I treated centrosymmetric-looking entries as effectively SHG-inactive, then favored acentric semiconducting chalcogenide/iodide frameworks with moderately small gaps and aligned polar units. Very ionic halides/alkali salts should be too small; Te/Hg/Tl/Nb-rich narrow-gap compounds often risk being much larger than 20 pm/V.

Most plausible near-20 candidates:

| rank | candidate | structural/chemical rationale | estimated largest \|dᵢⱼ\| |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | c006 | Acentric Ba/K gallium selenide-chloride network; BaGa–Se IR-NLO motifs similar to known ~20 pm/V gallium selenides | ~20.2 pm/V |
| 2 | c039 | Polar RbGeI₃-type lone-pair iodide; I gives strong polarizability but not as extreme as Te/Hg phases | ~19.5 pm/V |
| 3 | c093 | CuAlSe₂ chalcopyrite-like acentric selenide; classic tetrahedral semiconductor NLO chemistry | ~21 pm/V |
| 4 | c056 | Ag–In–Ge selenide stannite/chalcopyrite derivative; Ag/Se enhances response, likely slightly below/above 20 | ~18.7 pm/V |
| 5 | c038 | Polar Tl/Sb sulfide with stereochemically active lone pairs; sulfide gap keeps it near, not far above, 20 | ~21.8 pm/V |

Final: c006, c039, c093, c056, c038
